summary: Los Angeles County lookout tower built 1935 to replace a 1932 guard-station lookout; abandoned by 1947 over smog; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 lookout on a 10-foot open timber tower
facts.status_note: Register list shows Gone; removal date unknown; no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: no staffing record for the lookout found; a reminiscence describes the earlier Forest Service station crew of eight, including the cook

events.note: Guard station building built for double duty as a lookout site; the reminiscence describes a crew of eight at the station
Lookout built on a 10-foot open timber tower; replaced the earlier guard-station building

Registered March 11, 2020; nominated by Brad Eells

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the 1935 lookout replaced the earlier building, while the reminiscence says that building burned and was never rebuilt. These fit together: the station was not rebuilt, and the tower was put up in its place. The fire date is not given in any source read, so no fire event is recorded.

notes_for_editor: Most detail rests on one register page. Its account of the earlier station's fire and crew is a reminiscence (Jack Rimmer, paraphrased by John Damann, quoting a Harrison Irving Scott book), so it is secondhand and gives no year for the fire. The Ridge Route gallery describes the area above the road, not the lookout. The register credits photos and images to Jack Rimmer and Mike Guerin, but gives no image URLs, so no photo entries were added. No source says whether the site is public.
